subject.title: PR5/5 durable core: internal session delivery handoff

question: Should OpenClaw adopt and sequence this new opt-in durable-runtime, shared-state, protocol, and internal recovery architecture in core?
rationale: The PR creates a broad persistent runtime and public operator surface whose ownership, release sequencing, and long-term support cannot be decided from implementation correctness alone.

options.title: Sponsor and sequence the stack
options.body: Choose a canonical architecture issue, review the predecessor PRs in order, and require this PR to rebase to a focused final handoff with exact-head proof.

options.title: Narrow to existing recovery owners
options.body: Retain only a bounded session and restart recovery improvement using current queues and state owners, deferring the general durable runtime and protocol surfaces.

options.title: Decline the core architecture
options.body: Close the durable stack if maintainers do not want to own the new runtime, database, environment, and protocol contracts.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and sequence the stack
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical architecture issue, review the predecessor PRs in order, and require this PR to rebase to a focused final handoff with exact-head proof.
